### 2026-10-12 – This is my first entry for the new week 2. My Idea for this week was a nightlight in the form of one of those crystals, since I need a nightlight and I don't wanna buy one from Ikea. Today I made a BO

**2h**

This is my first entry for the new week 2. My Idea for this week was a nightlight in the form of one of those crystals, since I need a nightlight and I don't wanna buy one from Ikea. Today I made a BOM for all the hardware (Its not that much lowk)

1.4xAA battery holder

2.8.5X8.5MM 6Pin Push Tactile Power Micro Switch Self lock On/Off button Latching switch

3.5V LED_BRGK(RGB LED)

4.3 resistors, two 220ohm, one 270ohm(the red pin in the Led uses less power and thus needs more resistance

### 2026-10-12 – Today I finished the Schem AND Pcb Editor. This wasn't that big of a challenge, as I only have 6 symbols on the board and no microcontrollers. I did have a bit of a challenge to get the latch push swi

**2h**

Today I finished the Schem AND Pcb Editor. This wasn't that big of a challenge, as I only have 6 symbols on the board and no microcontrollers. I did have a bit of a challenge to get the latch push switch, as I want it to click and stay on until you click again, But it wasn't that hard.

### 2026-10-14 – I began working on the actual CAD for my diy nightlight project. For those who don't know, I'm designing a nightlight that is shaped like a crystal and turns on when you push down on it, sort of like

**4h**

I began working on the actual CAD for my diy nightlight project. For those who don't know, I'm designing a nightlight that is shaped like a crystal and turns on when you push down on it, sort of like this IKEA nightlights. today, I designed the base, where Im gonna put my PCB and battery holder, and managed to import a cool shape of a crystal. Though I did have a hard time trying to find out how to shell the crystal to hollow it out so that I can add an LED strip in it. I Did end up doing it, so now I just have to model the actual "clicking" part

### 2026-10-16 – So I kinda realized that making it so that you have to Push on the lamp is a lot harder than just adding a switch, so I have to redo some stuff. its not that big of a deal; I can just replace my old s

**3h**

So I kinda realized that making it so that you have to Push on the lamp is a lot harder than just adding a switch, so I have to redo some stuff. its not that big of a deal; I can just replace my old switch with a slider in the PCB or delete it and get a battery holder with a built in switch, and I didn't fully finished the Cad so I don't have to redo everything. Also, even though this isn't related to this week, I finally finished the Pcb of the yoto from week 1!

### 2026-10-17 – Im finished! (I hope). This should be my last entry, and I just wanted to add a final BOM to finish it

**3h**

Im finished! (I hope). This should be my last entry, and I just wanted to add a final BOM to finish it
I've decided my nightlight will be green, as red means I have to change the resistor (red LED's require less power)and I like green more than blue. BOM:

Red-Red-Brown-Gold resistor, or 220 ohms:E-Projects 10EP514220R 220 Ohm Resistors, 1/4 W, 5% (Pack of 10)

https://www.amazon.ca/Clearhill-Dimmable-320LEDs-Waterproof-Decoration/dp/B0CZ6SGWMX?source=ps-sl-shoppingads-lpcontext&ref_=fplfs&smid=A1NZ7LAJP641BP&th=1

5V USB COB GREEN LED Strip Lights

battery holder: DAIERTEK 4 AA Battery Holder with Switch 6V Battery Case Holder with Cover 4 Slots 1.5V AA Battery Storage Box with Wires Battery Connector -3pcs
